name: Softpedia

sources.title: Softpedia User Help — 'Software Submission': full form or PAD-file URL submission
Softpedia Submit Program page (403 to automated fetch; linked from site menubar)
Wikipedia — Softpedia overview: software download portal, editor-reviewed listings, PUP flagging

requirements: A downloadable software product (Windows, Mac, Linux, Mobile, Games — separate submit sections per platform)
Check via site search that the product isn't already listed before submitting
Two submission modes: fill the full form, or provide a PAD-file URL (preferred — Softpedia's automated monitoring picks up new versions from the PAD quickly)
preparation: Product name, download URL, short + long descriptions, category, publisher/contact email
Ideally a hosted PAD (Portable Application Description) XML file — submit once and updates propagate automatically
A clean installer — Softpedia flags adware/spyware/tie-in bundles as potentially unwanted and marks products accordingly
workflow: Search Softpedia to confirm the product isn't already listed
Open the Submit Program page (menubar link or /user/submit.shtml) — pick the right platform section
Either complete the full form or submit the PAD-file URL
Wait for editorial processing — third-party submit trackers report ~14 days; you get an email when published
Verify the product page is live in the correct Softpedia section
watchFor: Submit pages are per-platform — submitting a Windows app via the wrong section wastes the review cycle
Softpedia hosts binaries on its own servers and tests them; bundled offers/adware get your product marked as a PUP
The submit page 403s automated fetchers — use a real browser or submit the PAD URL
Registration is optional for downloads but the submission flow uses the publisher form
countsAsLive: A public product page under the relevant softpedia.com section (win/mac/linux/mobile/games) with download links and editor-tested status
unknowns: Exact review SLA for non-PAD submissions
Whether SaaS/web-only products without a downloadable binary are accepted (Softpedia historically lists web apps in some categories — unverified)
Whether the listing's developer-site link is dofollow
